title: Evaporative Emission Control System Malfunction
shortDescription: EVAP system has a general fault detected.
fullDescription: DTC P0440: EVAP system has a general fault detected. Codes in the P0440–P0479 range relate to the Evaporative Emission Control (EVAP) system, which captures fuel vapors and routes them to the engine for combustion.
safetyImpact: EVAP faults do not normally affect drivability or safety, but they will fail emissions tests and may cause a small fuel-economy loss.

causes.cause: Loose, cracked, or missing fuel cap

symptoms: No drivability symptoms in most cases

fixSteps.title: Inspect Fuel Cap
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and reinstall the gas cap until it clicks. Inspect seal for cracks or fuel residue.

fixSteps.title: Smoke Test EVAP System
fixSteps.instruction: Use an EVAP smoke machine to pressurize the system and locate leaks at hoses, canister, and tank.

fixSteps.title: Test Purge and Vent Solenoids
fixSteps.instruction: Command solenoids on/off with a bidirectional scan tool, listen for clicks, measure resistance.

fixSteps.title: Replace Failed Component
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the failed solenoid, hose, canister, or sensor identified during testing.

faq.q: Can I keep driving with an EVAP code?
faq.a: Yes — EVAP faults rarely affect drivability, but they will fail an emissions inspection and waste fuel vapors.

faq.q: Will a loose gas cap really set this?
faq.a: Yes — many EVAP small-leak codes (P0442, P0455, P0457) are caused by a gas cap that wasn't tightened until it clicked.

faq.q: Is this DIY-friendly?
faq.a: Cap and visible-hose fixes are easy. Locating small leaks usually requires a smoke machine.

fullDescription: DTC P0457: Loose or missing fuel cap reported by EVAP monitor. Codes in the P0440–P0479 range relate to the Evaporative Emission Control (EVAP) system, which captures fuel vapors and routes them to the engine for combustion.
safetyImpact: EVAP faults do not normally affect drivability or safety, but they will fail emissions tests and may cause a small fuel-economy loss.

causes.cause: Loose, cracked, or missing fuel cap

symptoms: No drivability symptoms in most cases

fixSteps.title: Inspect Fuel Cap
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and reinstall the gas cap until it clicks. Inspect seal for cracks or fuel residue.

fixSteps.title: Smoke Test EVAP System
fixSteps.instruction: Use an EVAP smoke machine to pressurize the system and locate leaks at hoses, canister, and tank.

fixSteps.title: Test Purge and Vent Solenoids
fixSteps.instruction: Command solenoids on/off with a bidirectional scan tool, listen for clicks, measure resistance.

fixSteps.title: Replace Failed Component
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the failed solenoid, hose, canister, or sensor identified during testing.

faq.q: Can I keep driving with an EVAP code?
faq.a: Yes — EVAP faults rarely affect drivability, but they will fail an emissions inspection and waste fuel vapors.

faq.q: Will a loose gas cap really set this?
faq.a: Yes — many EVAP small-leak codes (P0442, P0455, P0457) are caused by a gas cap that wasn't tightened until it clicked.

faq.q: Is this DIY-friendly?
faq.a: Cap and visible-hose fixes are easy. Locating small leaks usually requires a smoke machine.
